faq.a: Yasemin is associated with the Arabic form يَاسَمِين, whose core sense is yasemin; jasmine (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Yasemin?
faq.a: Yasemin is associated with Arabic. Yasemin is the Turkish form of Arabic يَاسْمِين (Yāsmīn), the word for the jasmine flower.
Yes — the underlying form يَاسَمِين is Arabic.
Yasemin can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Yasemin should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Yāsmīn is not a Quranic personal name.

A romanized syllable approximation is ya-se-min. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Yasemin?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Yasemin, yasemin. Script forms are يَاسَمِين, یاسمین, यासमीन.

faq.q: Is Yasemin a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
